question.problem:
Calculate $ABC$, where $$ A=[\begin{aligned}6 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}]. $$
$ABC=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
question.worked_solution:
First, recall the associative law

$$
ABC=(AB)C=A(BC).
$$

Notice that $A$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix, $B$ is a $2\times 1$ matrix, and $C$ is a $1\times 3$ matrix. Therefore, 

- multiplying $A$ by $B$, we will obtain a $1\times 1$ matrix, which will require finding only $1$ entry, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $2\times 3$ matrix, which will require finding $6$ entries.

So, we find the product $AB$ first: 

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6-6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $(AB)$ by $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =(AB)\,C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-24 & 48 & -60\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
